# Stop the Data Sync schedules in the engine: the corpus is leaving this repo

## Context

`data-sync-pipeline` has failed on **30 consecutive hourly runs**. `data-sync-watchdog` has answered by posting **61 bot comments** onto the standing alarm #17834. Both are running on a schedule right now, and neither can succeed, because the thing they measure was deliberately removed.

@neo-opus-grace priced this exactly on [#17416 comment 5531512260](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17416#issuecomment-5531512260) and routed it to the operator as a Tier-4 fork, option 4: *"Accept the staleness deliberately — then the honest follow-through is to stop the schedule, because an alarm on a condition nobody is permitted to fix is noise, and #17834's comment ratio is the receipt."*

@tobiu ruled option 4 on 2026-09-08. This ticket executes that ruling and nothing else.

## The Problem

The repo split (`c623b2f63c`, #17791/#17806) removed the corpus-generation stage as collateral — it invoked `./ai/scripts/maintenance/syncGithubWorkflow.mjs`, an engine `ai/` path the split deleted. Corpus production stopped on 2026-08-26.

The destination for that producer is **not** this repository. Per D#17247 row 6, D#17846, and Epic #17416, GitHub conversation markdown moves to a dedicated content-sync repo, and consumers acquire it through a gitignored installer on the skills precedent. The operator's standing constraint: **markdown must never be synced into engine, brain, or other repos directly** — it is pure churn that makes every repo statistic read as bloat. `resources/content/**` is **17,929 tracked files** in this repo today.

`f809d86e29` (#17920/#17927) then added `assertCorpusFreshness`, which correctly turned a silently-green pipeline red. **That guard is right and stays.** A pipeline deriving portal artifacts from a frozen corpus was worse than one that refuses. But it is now instrumenting a pipeline that should not be scheduled in this repository at all — so the guard reports truthfully, hourly, into a lane with no lawful implementation path (#17920 is closed; #17416 is `[PROVISIONAL_UNGRADUATED: D#17247]` and by its own header not implementation-authorizing).

## The Architectural Reality

| surface | measured |
|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/data-sync-pipeline.yml` | `schedule: cron '0 * * * *'` — hourly |
| `.github/workflows/data-sync-watchdog.yml` | `schedule: cron '20 * * * *'` — hourly |
| `assertCorpusFreshness` | defined `buildScripts/dataSyncPipeline.mjs:697`, called `:781` |
| the step it fails in | `Run bounded Data Sync emission and publish` |
| the step after it | `Push Data to neomjs/pages` — **never reached since the guard landed** |
| last `neomjs/pages` publish | 2026-08-31T11:35:45Z |
| `f809d86e29` (guard) committed | 2026-08-31T11:52:03Z — **17 minutes later** |

**So stopping the schedule removes 24 failing runs per day plus hourly ticket spam, and removes nothing that currently works.** Pages has been frozen for 8 days independently of this change.

**One measured absence worth recording:** no commit has ever removed either `schedule:` block — `git log` on both workflow files shows the pipeline's last substantive edit at 2026-08-20 and the watchdog untouched by anything but dependabot since Phoebe created it (`05ef28a9ad`). Whatever form the earlier disable took, **it left no durable artifact in the workflow files.** That absence is observed, not explained — I am not asserting a mechanism for it. It is the reason this ticket makes the stop in git: a decision that lives only in a runtime toggle reads as an unattended defect to the next seat, and gets "repaired".

## The Fix

1. `.github/workflows/data-sync-pipeline.yml` — drop the `schedule:` block; keep `workflow_dispatch`.
2. `.github/workflows/data-sync-watchdog.yml` — drop the `schedule:` block; keep `workflow_dispatch`.
3. Both keep a header comment naming #17416 as the destination lane, so the next reader finds the decision instead of re-deriving it.
4. Close #17834 with the ruling recorded on it.

Manual dispatch is retained deliberately: #17416 will need to exercise both surfaces during its cutover, and deleting the workflows would make that a restore instead of a run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Neither workflow file contains a `schedule:` key; `git show origin/dev:<path> | grep -c 'cron'` returns `0` for both.
- [ ] Both files retain `workflow_dispatch`.
- [ ] **Re-enable first:** `gh workflow enable` both workflows so each reads `active`. At 2026-09-08T05:33Z I disabled both in the Actions UI as an interim stop (the merge gate is human-owned and the alarm was commenting hourly). A disabled workflow emits no scheduled run *whatever the file says*, so without this step the next criterion would pass on an empty diff — a control that cannot fail.
- [ ] `gh run list --workflow data-sync-pipeline.yml` shows no new scheduled run after the merge commit's timestamp, with the workflow `active`. *(post-merge; verify ≥70 min after re-enabling to clear one full cron window)*
- [ ] #17834 is CLOSED and carries a comment naming the ruling, this ticket, and #17416.
- [ ] `buildScripts/dataSyncPipeline.mjs` is unmodified — the freshness guard is untouched.
- [ ] `resources/content/**` is unmodified — file count stays 17,929.

## Out of Scope

- **Removing `resources/content/**` from this repo.** 17,929 files with live consumers (portal `TreeList.mjs`, KB `sourcePaths`, `check-chore-sync.mjs`, `TicketSource`). That deletion is #17416's, sequenced behind the dedicated repo existing.
- **Relaxing or removing `assertCorpusFreshness`.** Explicitly refused — see Avoided Traps.
- **The §8.3a `repoSlug` re-key.** Ruled in D#17846, unimplemented, untouched here.
- **Deciding the corpus destination.** D#17247 OQ6 is `[OQ_RESOLUTION_PENDING]`; nothing here pre-commits it.
- **`neomjs/pages` publication.** Frozen since 2026-08-31 by the guard, not by this change. If Pages needs to advance before #17416 lands, that is its own ticket with its own evidence.

## Avoided Traps

- **Silencing by widening the corpus-age band.** #17920's Avoided Traps names this; Grace refused it twice. A shorter green run is not a fix. This ticket stops the *schedule*, and leaves the guard's verdict intact for whenever the pipeline is dispatched.
- **Deleting the workflows.** Would turn #17416's cutover rehearsal into a restore-from-history exercise.
- **Disabling in the Actions UI.** Invisible to `git log`, and therefore invisible to the next seat reading the repo. The measured absence above is the argument for doing it in git.
- **Treating the red as a defect to repair.** It is a guard working correctly. The ticket that "fixes" it by making it green would rebuild the thing the split removed on purpose — the failure mode Grace recorded on 2026-09-06 as *"a disabled mechanism is a decision artifact; find the decision that removed it before restoring it."*

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with` #17416 / D#17846 §8.3a. No ADR is amended, superseded, or challenged: this changes a schedule, not a contract.

## Post-merge validation complete — and AC-4 was measured with its confound removed

All seven criteria verified against merged `dev`, not from session state.

| AC | result |
|---|---|
| 1 — no `schedule:` key | `grep -c cron` = **0** in both workflow files on `dev` |
| 2 — `workflow_dispatch` retained | present in both |
| 3 — **re-enable first** | both returned to `active` at **2026-09-08T07:50:36Z** |
| 4 — no scheduled run | **0 scheduled runs in the 3h38m since**, workflows active throughout |
| 5 — #17834 closed with the ruling | closed `COMPLETED` on the merge; the ruling comment it lacked is now at [issuecomment-5581332155](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17834#issuecomment-5581332155) |
| 6 — guard untouched | `assertCorpusFreshness` present on `dev` |
| 7 — corpus untouched | 17,929 files |

**AC-4's ordering was load-bearing and nearly went wrong.** I had disabled both workflows in the Actions UI at 05:33Z as an interim stop, and a disabled workflow emits no scheduled run *whatever the file says* — so had I checked AC-4 without re-enabling, it would have passed identically on an empty diff. AC-3 exists to remove that confound and it is why the two are ordered.

The window is also comfortably wider than specified: the criterion asked for ≥70 minutes to clear one cron cycle. **3h38m elapsed**, and both workflows were hourly, so roughly three runs each would have fired had the crons survived. Last actual scheduled runs remain `data-sync-pipeline` **04:05:47Z** and `data-sync-watchdog` **04:45:57Z**, both predating the merge at 05:53:56Z.

**Zero new bot comments on #17834** since it closed — the hourly accrual that reached 61 comments has stopped at its source rather than been muted.

**AC-5 was half-met on merge and is now whole.** The alarm auto-closed two seconds after #18451 merged but carried no explanation, so a ten-day, 61-comment alarm would have gone silent with nothing in the record saying why. That is the exact failure this ticket was filed against — a decision that leaves no durable artifact reads as an unattended defect to the next seat. The closure comment carries the ruling, its source, what deliberately did *not* change (the freshness guard, the corpus, the refusal to widen the band), and the honest re-fire trigger: #17416 delivering a producer, never a re-added cron.
